Evaluate curves on a new grid using a B-spline basis

Source: R/dense_data.R
dense_data.Rd

Converts discretely sampled curves to functional data with an fda B-spline basis, then evaluates the fitted functions at an evenly spaced grid over the original domain. The output grid may be denser or sparser than the input grid. Input and output matrices have evaluation points in rows and curves in columns.

Usage

dense_data(data, num_evaluation)

Arguments

data

Finite numeric matrix with at least two evaluation points in rows and one curve per column.

num_evaluation

Integer of at least two giving the number of points in the output grid.

Value

A numeric matrix with num_evaluation rows and one column per input curve.

Details

The input domain is assumed to be the equally spaced sequence from zero to nrow(data) - 1. The B-spline basis is created from that domain and passed explicitly to fda::Data2fd().

Examples

set.seed(123)
generated <- gaussian_curves_generator(
  sample_size = 5,  # number of curves
  num_points = 101, # original evaluation points per curve
  mu = 0,           # target mean
  sig = 1,          # target standard deviation
  fwhm = 20         # smoothing FWHM used to generate the curves
)
dense_curves <- dense_data(data = generated$curves, num_evaluation = 200)
dim(dense_curves) # 200 5
#> [1] 200   5
